related_questions.question: What is the most successful treatment for gastric cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: For early-stage gastric cancer, surgery, particularly gastrectomy (removal of part or all of the stomach), is often the most successful treatment, potentially offering a cure. For advanced or recurrent gastric cancer, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and chemotherapy are frequently used, either alone or in combination with surgery.
snippet_highlighted_words: surgery, particularly gastrectomy (removal of part or all of the stomach)

list.title: Surgery (Gastrectomy):
list.snippet: This is the primary curative treatment for early-stage gastric cancer, aiming to remove the tumor and surrounding tissue to prevent spread.

list.title: Endoscopic Resection:
list.snippet: For very small, early-stage tumors, endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) or endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) may be sufficient, especially if the tumor hasn't invaded the stomach wall.

list.title: Chemotherapy and/or Radiation Therapy (Before or After Surgery):
list.snippet: These may be used in conjunction with surgery to help shrink the tumor, destroy cancer cells, and prevent recurrence.

list.title: Chemotherapy:
list.snippet: Chemotherapy is often the first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic gastric cancer.

list.title: Immunotherapy:
list.snippet: Drugs like nivolumab and pembrolizumab, which are PD-1 inhibitors, have shown promise in improving survival rates for advanced or recurrent gastric cancer.

list.title: Targeted Therapy:
list.snippet: Drugs like trastuzumab (for HER2-positive tumors) and ramucirumab (for certain advanced cases) target specific molecules involved in cancer growth.

list.title: Combination Therapies:
list.snippet: Treatment often involves a combination of chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and/or targeted therapy, depending on the individual patient and tumor characteristics.

list.title: Radiation Therapy:
list.snippet: May be used to relieve symptoms or shrink tumors, particularly in advanced cases.

list.title: Stage of Cancer:
list.snippet: The stage of gastric cancer (how far it has spread) is a key factor in determining the most appropriate treatment approach.

list.title: Patient's Overall Health:
list.snippet: A patient's overall health and fitness level are also important considerations when choosing a treatment plan.

list.title: Tumor Characteristics:
list.snippet: Specific molecular characteristics of the tumor (like HER2 status) can influence treatment choices.

text_blocks.snippet: A multidisciplinary team, including surgeons, oncologists, radiation oncologists, and other specialists, is crucial for developing an effective and personalized treatment plan for gastric cancer.
